A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FK-PINN research and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. The complete appendices match in extracted text and rendered appearance, supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original PDE-solving experiments in Section 7 and Appendix E, including numerical errors, optimizer comparisons, loss-landscape analyses, and Monte Carlo budget sensitivity.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and their numerical and graphical results in Section 7 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The Monte Carlo estimator, augmented FK-PINN objective, adaptive loss weighting, and training procedure in Sections 3–4 and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same Poisson, Schrödinger-type, mean escape time, and committor problems under the same domains and conditions. The new discussion of neural operators does not introduce an evaluated task.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain standard PINNs and, in Appendix E.4, ENGD and Adam + L-BFGS + NNCG. The newly cited works are discussed as related research, not evaluated as additional baselines.

E3.justification: Experimental settings remain identical, including four hidden layers of 128 tanh neurons, 30,000 Adam followed by 15,000 L-BFGS iterations, and the L2 and H1 metrics. Appendix E retains the same sampling and Monte Carlo settings.

E4.justification: Appendices E.3 and E.5 retain the same Hessian-conditioning analysis, loss-landscape visualizations, and sensitivity studies of time step, trajectory count, and supervision proportion. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Tables 1 and 4 retain the statement that results average five independent runs with different random seeds. The plus/minus reporting and graphical uncertainty displays are unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported numerical values, plotted results, and findings are unchanged throughout Section 7 and Appendix E. For example, Table 1 retains Schrödinger-type relative L2 errors of 0.624 ± 0.195 for PINNs and 0.096 ± 0.010 for FK-PINNs.

T1.justification: The assumptions, definitions, conditioning guarantees, error bounds, and proofs in Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–D are unchanged. The added reference to Li et al.'s Theorem 5.1 is literature discussion, not a new or revised mathematical result in this work.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions in Section 1.3, and conclusion retain the same claims about FK supervision, operator preconditioning, non-asymptotic error bounds, derivative pseudo-dimension bounds, and empirical performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations and limitations remain unchanged, including the conditioning explanation, error saturation with fixed sparse supervision, and the accuracy–cost tradeoffs and coarse-discretization failures discussed in Appendix E.5.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, label-generation instructions, training schedules, and runtime information are retained unchanged. No code or data access information is added.

R1.justification: Section 2.4 adds a focused paragraph crediting earlier noisy-supervision work by Li et al. (2023) and the already-cited Heldmann et al. (2023), acknowledging Li et al.'s training guarantee, and discussing Viswanath et al. (2026). Two references are added, clarifying the relationship of the retained any-source conditioning and end-to-end analysis to prior work.

P1.justification: The principal prose addition is the weak-supervision paragraph in Section 2.4. Section 7.2 also gains an explicit Table 1 reference; the remaining narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: The added paragraph causes limited page reflow, moving the starts of Sections 4 and 6 to subsequent pages and adjusting surrounding spacing. Figures, tables, captions, and graphical content are retained without redesign.

improvement.justification: V2 improves scholarly attribution by explicitly acknowledging earlier noisy-supervision methods and a prior training guarantee in Section 2.4. This makes the relationship between existing approaches and the paper's theoretical contributions clearer. The improvement is limited because the methods, proofs, experimental evidence, and limitations remain unchanged.
